doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Walking out of Miles's second session
summary: McLean explains leaving the session after a mistake and Miles's pee-pee jibe.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Was J. R. Monterose in the studio as well?
No. Not that I remember. I never even . . .
The second date that you did with Miles, he did two of your pieces, Dr. Jackle and Minor March. But you’re not on the other tunes.
Right. I just walked out. I left the studio.
What was . . . ? – tell us that story.

Because Miles had – first of all, when I got there, I felt like I was an outcast in some kind of way. This is after I had been working with Miles for a number of years. Finally he said something. I kept running down, making a mistake on one of them tunes, Itty Bitty or one of them tunes there. I made a mistake once. They had to stop and start again. He said, “What’s the matter with you? We’ll start it again.” Did it again, made a mistake. Then he said, “Hey, what’s the matter, Jackie? You got to pee? Got to pee pee?” Aw man, when he said that, that really got me mad. So I said, “Yeah, and I’m going home to do it,” and I packed up my horn and split, went out the door. That was it.
